name: Crash Twinsanity
description: Crash Twinsanity running natively on your computer, made from the game's own code. You need your own disc; nothing from it is in this application.

disc.plays_note: This version of the game plays the PAL disc (SLES-52568) and the North American disc (SLUS-20909).

vita.label: PS Vita
note: Copy {vpk} to the PS Vita and install it with VitaShell.
Copy the folder {data_dir} from the PS Vita folder to the PS Vita's memory card, so that it is {data} there: the settings, the mods and disc-image.txt.
Copy your own disc image to {data}/{disc} on the PS Vita. The launcher never copies the disc image.
The PS Vita needs its shader library ur0:data/libshacccg.suprx -- the usual homebrew step. The launcher never downloads or carries this file.
discs_note: {disc_file} names the disc the game starts: the launcher writes it for the disc you chose (Settings > Disc image), so copy that disc to {data} under the name it gives, {disc}.

The European and the North American discs can live side by side on the PS Vita, for example as game.iso and ntsc.iso: write the name of the one to play in {data}/{disc_file}. The North American disc runs at 60 Hz and keeps its own memory card.
vita.mods_note: On the PS Vita, mods are switched here and copied: after you add or switch a mod, press Make the PS Vita folder again (here or in Settings), then copy {data_dir} to the PS Vita's memory card.
about: Choose PS Vita with Get the game for PS Vita or another computer on the Games page: the launcher puts the PS Vita version in a folder named vita inside your game folder.
Install {vpk} from that folder with VitaShell; the PS Vita also needs ur0:data/libshacccg.suprx, which the launcher never carries.
Copy the folder's {data_dir} to the PS Vita's memory card: it holds your settings, the language packs, the mods you switched on and {disc_file}.
Copy your own disc image to {data} under the name {disc_file} gives; the European and the North American discs can sit side by side, as game.iso and ntsc.iso, and {disc_file} chooses between them.
Mods are added and switched here on a computer, never on the PS Vita: after a change, press Make the PS Vita folder again and copy {data_dir} once more.
Your saves stay on the PS Vita, in {data}/memcards; the North American disc keeps its own card beside it.

folder.name: vita
folder.why: the PS Vita folder: <game folder>/vita holds the package, README-vita.txt and ux0/data/twinsanity (the console's data folder as its memory card has it) with the game folder's ps2r.ini without the computer's own keys (its folders, its picture size, window, vertical sync and frame rate, and its game rate: the PS Vita has its own default -- the PAL disc's 50 Hz), a copy of the language packs and of the mods switched on, and disc-image.txt naming the disc's file name (game.iso when it is not a plain name)

game_folder.settings_header: # ps2r.ini -- Crash Twinsanity's settings. The launcher's Settings page and the game's Options menu both edit this file.

settings.note: These are the settings the game shows under Options, kept in ps2r.ini in the game folder. A change here is a change there.

rows.label: Text language
rows.help: The game's text: every language your disc has text in, and the translations in the game folder's mods folder.

rows.label: Speech language
rows.help: The voices, the movies' sound and the title cards: every language your disc has speech in.

rows.label: Game rate
rows.help: 60 is the default. 50 is the speed of a PAL console. Takes effect the next time the game starts.

rows.label: Aspect ratio
rows.help: Auto is the TV's 4:3; the wide shapes widen the picture the way the game's own widescreen option does.

rows.label: Internal scale
rows.help: How many times the PlayStation 2's resolution the game is drawn at.

rows.label: Texture filter
rows.help: Original is what the game asked the console for.

rows.label: Vertical sync
rows.help: Waits for the display between frames. With a frame rate above 60 the display's refresh is the effective cap.

rows.label: Frame rate
rows.help: The game always runs at its normal speed. 30 shows every other picture; 60 every picture; above 60 the pictures in between are blended. Uncapped shows as many as your computer can and turns vertical sync off.

rows.label: FPS counter
rows.help: The pictures shown per second, top right, in the game's own lettering.

rows.label: Frame rate on PS Vita
rows.help: Used when this ps2r.ini is copied to ux0:data/twinsanity/ on the PS Vita. Auto runs at 60 while the PS Vita keeps up and holds a steady 30 when it cannot.

rows.label: Memory cards
rows.help: Your saves. Inside the game folder unless you move them.

rows.label: Disc image
rows.help: The disc the game starts with when you open it without the launcher.

builtin.name: Level select
builtin.author: TwinsanityEvolved
builtin.help: A list of every level, boss and area, started at once.

builtin.name: Speedrun mode
builtin.author: TwinsanityEvolved
builtin.help: A real-time timer at the top of the screen and practice save states (F9 / F10 / F11).
